title: I ran an LLM trading agent 24/7 for a month. 107 trades later, I'm down 1%, and it didn't even fully follow my own strategy.
author: ruby-cos
selftext:
Curious how people here are actually using AI in their trading workflow right now. Is it mostly for research and data gathering, or are people letting it make real decisions?

Some background: I've been trading for about 2 years, mostly spot, and recently started looking into automation. I tried a third party platform where you write out your strategy and pick an LLM model, and it claims to run a 24/7 agent for you on Hyperliquid, with the LLM analyzing market conditions to decide entries and exits.

Since setting the agent up on 7/24, it's completed 107 trades total. Mixed wins and losses, currently sitting at about 1% down, mostly eaten by fees rather than bad calls.

The bigger issue for me is that the LLM seems to hallucinate or act on its own judgment sometimes. It's not executing my strategy exactly as written, which has made me pretty uneasy about trusting the platform. I genuinely can't tell if the underperformance is because my strategy itself isn't good, or if using an LLM to actually execute trades is just fundamentally unreliable right now.

**So I'm trying to figure out if AI is actually useful for trading (stocks or crypto), or if I just haven't found the right way to apply it yet. How is everyone here actually using it in practice?**

replies.author: ruby-cos
replies.body:
No, but yours looks worth trying too! Are yours also using an LLM for the actual trading decisions? How do you make sure the LLM agent is 100% following your strategy and not going rogue on its own? 

I guess hallucinations are just something that's bound to happen with LLMs, we just never know when it's going to hit 😭

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body:
Yes it's exactly that. LLMs trade for you on Hyperliquid. I didn't know there were others haha!

You can check the leaderboard, some bots are doing very well for the past week. I added the ability to do deep trade chain analytics so you can tune your bot with Codex or Claude Code based on its strengths and weaknesses.

https://vtxmacro.com/leaderboard?t=30d&page=1

To answer your question, yes LLMs can make mistakes and they are not guaranteed to follow instructions. I have this issue with the free Gemma 4 31B models I use. 

But I have also started testing bots running GPT 5.6 Sol through headless Codex, hopefully they trade better and follow instructions better.

The market you trade matters a lot, if you pick a hot, volatile market they will do well assuming that your model and instructions are good. Right now I'm focusing on trading AI and RAM stocks so NBIS, SanDisk, Samsung, Micron, etc. They are all available on HL as perps.

comments.author: peeeanuts
comments.body: I think the useful split is letting the model do research, not execution. I’m building OpenCandle around that. It pulls filings, news and market context together, then I decide what to do with it.

comments.author: Ok-Draft2744
comments.body:
I've got very similar results to yours, trading for about 6 months now. Its mostly an experiment for me, and iteratively trying to improve it. I find it follows trends well but the market has been choppy this year so fairly flst results. I am just glad it's not losing money. 

It mostly does what I am asking it to do as long as it is simple, exit/stop loss decisions are all in code to make sure it never goes down too much. I find Grok works well for that, but to be honest others will likely yield similar results. Claude is a bit kore opinionated and more likely to diverge. The gpt family are also fairly well behaved
